tweets: Calling external contracts risks losing control flow before your function finishes.
A malicious contract can reenter your code mid-execution, causing interactions to behave undesirably.
The best practice is to perform all internal state changes before making any external calls.
OpenZeppelin's ReentrancyGuard is cited as an example of such a mechanism.
This ordering prevents the attacker from taking control during your function's execution.
